{{- /* Wrap tables so wide ones scroll horizontally on mobile instead of being clipped by main's overflow-x-hidden. Sideways scrolling is a poor answer for wide data tables though: a five-column props table forces ~950px of content through a ~360px viewport, so the description column collapses to a sliver and rows grow hundreds of pixels tall. Tables with three or more columns therefore also get `table-stack`, which restacks each row as a labelled card below the md breakpoint (see main.css) — the header text rides along on each cell as `data-label`. Narrow tables read fine as tables at any width and are left alone. API member tables get `props-table` on top of that: main.css gives them a fixed layout so they always fit their container instead of scrolling sideways, and the toggle below collapses them to the first few rows. This family is not one shape. Across the site the same kind of table appears as `Parameter | Type | Description`, `Property | Modifiers | Type | Description`, `Name | Required? | Type | Description` (the legacy /latest/ props tables), `Prop | Type | Required | Description | Inherited from` (generated) and several more, so matching on the first header missed most of them. The one thing they all share is a `Type` column, and no ordinary content table on the site has one — that is the test. The generated dashboard event and command tables (dashboard-catalog-markdown.html) join by their `Type guard` / `Create with` column instead. Column order varies between the shapes, so widths are emitted per header name rather than by position; an unrecognised header is left to size itself from whatever share is left. The button ships hidden and is enabled by initPropsTable, so with no JS every row stays visible rather than being locked away behind dead UI. */ -}} {{- $headers := slice -}} {{- with .THead -}} {{- range index . 0 -}} {{- $headers = $headers | append (.Text | plainify | strings.TrimSpace) -}} {{- end -}} {{- end -}} {{- $isApi := false -}} {{- if ge (len $headers) 3 -}} {{- if or (in $headers "Type") (in $headers "Type guard") (in $headers "Create with") -}}{{- $isApi = true -}}{{- end -}} {{- end -}} {{- $widths := dict "Prop" "18%" "Name" "18%" "Parameter" "18%" "Property" "18%" "Field" "18%" "Member" "16%" "Method" "18%" "Type" "24%" "Required" "9%" "Required?" "9%" "Modifiers" "11%" "Default" "12%" "Description" "34%" "Notes" "34%" "Inherited from" "15%" "Value" "14%" "Event" "36%" "Command" "36%" "Type guard" "30%" "Create with" "30%" -}} {{- $noun := "rows" -}} {{- if $isApi -}} {{- $nouns := dict "Prop" "props" "Name" "props" "Parameter" "parameters" "Property" "properties" "Field" "fields" "Member" "members" "Event" "events" "Command" "commands" -}} {{- with index $nouns (index $headers 0) }}{{ $noun = . }}{{ end -}} {{- end -}}
{{- range .THead }} {{- range $i, $cell := . }} {{- $style := "" }} {{- with $cell.Alignment }}{{ $style = printf "text-align: %s;" . }}{{ end }} {{- if $isApi }}{{ with index $widths (index $headers $i) }}{{ $style = printf "%s width: %s;" $style . }}{{ end }}{{ end }} {{- /* The whole attribute is emitted via safeHTMLAttr: composing the value in a variable first makes Go's contextual escaper give up and write ZgotmplZ, and safeCSS alone does not satisfy it here. Both halves are ours — Goldmark's left/center/right, and the width table above. */}} {{ $cell.Text }} {{- end }} {{- end }} {{- range .TBody }} {{- range $i, $cell := . }} {{- $label := "" }} {{- if lt $i (len $headers) }}{{ $label = index $headers $i }}{{ end }} {{ $cell.Text }} {{- end }} {{- end }}
{{- if $isApi }} {{- end }}
